This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Order (revised
September 22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote,
and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/Virtua!Meeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bsaleaumua @malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state oflocal emergency, as well
as states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of California, and a
federal emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading
COVID-19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in
person would present imminent risks to. the health or safety of attendees. This way the public, the staff,
and the Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which
are not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although
no action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak
during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to
speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and
follow the directions for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are
not subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been
submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public
comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
BSaleaumua@malibucitv.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist
you. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate
in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-
2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

  Chair Cherin called the meeting to order at 9:03 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Lotte Cherin; Vice Chair Fireball Lawrence; Commissioners Barry

  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM I  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Recreation Manager Gallo administered the Oath of Office to Ex-Officio Clifford.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  John Mazza stated communication between the Parks and Recreation Commission
  and Planning Commission were essential to understand priorities, zoning issues,
  and restrictions before proposing an Arts Center.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked Mr. Mazza for his comments.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  1.  Arts in Education

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops were
  held at all Malibu schools in the Santa-Monica Malibu Unified School
  District. She stated staff were compiling poems and artist agreements for
  the 2023 Student Poetry and Art Anthology.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Commissioner Holland stated the spring art exhibition would include
  artwork by Jane Seymour. She stated the Commission would host a closing
  reception in June 2023.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the Jane Seymour exhibition would have
  freestanding pieces. He stated the Pep Williams art exhibition opening
  reception would take place on March 26, 2023 at 12:00 PM and the event
  included live music and a temporary display of artwork by Malibu Arts
  Association. He stated he worked with staff to install new gallery signs.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the Public Works Commission discussed a
  Neighborhood Beautification Program during the January 25, 2023 Regular
  meeting. He stated he would work with staff to obtain additional
  information on the Art in Public Places Ordinance.

  4.  Social Media

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked staff for consistent postings on social media.

  5.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the City Attorney was reviewing the
  Cooperative Agreement, which must be done before City Council approves
  the project.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  Page 3 of 5

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Vice Chair Lawrence stated the
  artwork would be completed before construction on the tunnel was finished.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Commissioner Haldeman seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  I.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the January 24, 2023
  Malibu Arts Commission Regular meeting.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu Arts Budget
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Proposed Malibu Arts Budget for Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Jones, Vice Chair Lawrence stated artists should
  select their frames and pay for framing expenses if they want their work showcased
  in the Malibu City Gallery.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Vice Chair Lawrence.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Chair Cherin stated the Commission could
  request additional funding from City Council at mid-year.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the Commission and staff had successfully worked
  within the parameters of the current budget.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staffing allocations were determined by City management. She stated poetry
  broadsides were Poet Laureate poems with a visual art element. She stated the Poet
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of February 28, 2023
  Page 4 of 5

  Laureate hosted quarterly poetry events typically with an open mic session and a
  featured reader, and poetry would be displayed in City parks.

  B.  Malibu Arts Center Survey Results
  Recommended Action: 1) Review and discuss the results of the Malibu Arts Center
  Survey; and 2) Provide a recommendation regarding the Malibu Arts Center for
  City Council consideration.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Chair Cherin, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the Arts Center was not on 2022-2023 City Council work plan. She stated City
  Council planned to discuss 2023-2024 priorities at a Special meeting on March 22,
  2023. She stated the recommendation provided by the Commission would be
  provided to City Council for consideration.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Acting Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the City Council Special meeting on March 22, 2023 was open to the
  public.

  John Mazza stated the Arts Center was not on the City Council work plan because
  it was not a priority, and the project should be reviewed by City Council and the
  Planning Commission.

  Vice Chair Lawrence thanked Mr. Mazza for his comments and requested him to
  submit recommendations on ways to progress the Arts Center project.

  Mr. Mazza stated the survey results were one-sided and a professional surveyor was
  needed for a proper community study.

  Ex-Officio Clifford stated indicated disagreement with Mr. Mazza. He stated the
  initial low-cost survey was needed to determine a general consensus for City
  Council consideration.

  Commissioner Holland stated the Commission distributed the survey to gather
  initial information for City Council consideration. She stated the survey served its
  purpose to begin the discussion of an Arts Center.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Commissioner Holland.

MOTION  Chair Cherin moved, and Vice Chair Lawrence seconded a motion to provide City
  Council with a recommendation to consider Malibu Arts Center. The question was
  called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated the Commission received
  compliments on the mid-year report from City Council during the February 27,

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated he worked on a documentary film "21 Miles in Malibu"

  for a potential showing at Malibu Bluffs Park.

  Commissioner Holland stated she was collecting art supply donations for students
  in Malawi, Africa.

  In response to Ex-Officio Clifford, Vice Chair Lawrence stated he would review
  the potential of photographer Julie Ellerton as an exhibitor for a single artist show
  at the Malibu City Gallery.

DISCUSSION: Each year in June, Council approves Commission assignments for the
upcoming Fiscal Year. The Commission is asked to review the current list of assignments
for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 (Attachment 1) and make recommendations for new and
revised assignments for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

Once approved by the Commission , the recommended assignments will be taken to
Council for review and approval.

ATTACHMENT: Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Commission Work Assignments

  Page 1 of 1  Agenda Item #5.A.
   City of Malibu
  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Members of the Malibu Arts Commission
FROM:  Steve McClary, City Manager
DATE:  June 16, 2022
SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Commission Assignments

At its Regular meeting on June 13, 2022, the City Council approved the following assignments for the Malibu
Arts Commission in Fiscal Year 2022-2023:
  1. Facilitate regular art exhibitions and related events at City facilities and businesses
  2. Review and recommend policies, procedures, and projects in accordance with the Art inPublic
  Places Ordinance
  3. Provide feedback regarding advertising, marketing, website content on the Malibu Arts
  Commission website and arts programs and events within Malibu and outside City limits
  (revised)
  4. Work with staff to facilitate arts programs, screenings, and events, including Arts in Education
  outreach in Malibu schools and partnerships with local organizations such as the Malibu Film
  Society (revised)
  5. Provide opportunities for and coordinate meetings with Malibu business owners and artists to promote,
  recognize, invest, and exhibit local artists
  6. Provide feedback regarding updates for arts events, programs and projects
  7. Review and provide feedback regarding Commission branding (revised)
  8. Assist Planning staff on the development of a Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) regarding thedisplay of
  art throughout the City
  9. Provide input regarding the current Temporary Use Permit process to allow temporary pop-up
  galleries, performances, screenings, and events in spaces in Malibu (revised)
  10. Explore a Performing Arts Center and advise the City Council on Commission recommendations
  (revised)
  11. Explore an Artist in Residence Program
  12. Explore opportunities for a professional arts consultant to work with the Arts Commission
  13. Develop relationships with commissions from other cities to exchange ideas and explore a partnership
  event (new)
  14. Explore the development of a Malibu creative directory (new)
  15. Make oral reports as needed to the City Council on Commission activities
  16. Submit a mid-year written report to the City Council on Commission activity

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  I.  Arts in Education

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo stated poetry workshops took
  place at all Malibu public schools, and the Student Art and Poetry
  Anthology would be completed in May 2023.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Commissioner Holland thanked Chair Cherin and Commission Haldeman
  for attending the Pep Williams art exhibition opening reception.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated the question and answer session with Pep
  Williams was great, and he enjoyed the event. He stated he was looking
  forward to the Jane Seymour art exhibition in May 2023.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  Commissioner Haldeman stated the Chamber of Commerce had been
  working on the Malibu Arts Festival, and he was supporting the Malibu Art
  Association event on April I and 2, 2023.

  Commissioner Jones stated Artificial Intelligence (AI) was present in art.

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated exploring AI could be a new way to share art
  by the Commission.

  Chair Cherin requested artwork related to AI be placed on a future agenda
  for further discussion.

  4.  Social Media

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated consistency was essential to gain a presence on
  social media, and staff had continued to add information on social media
  platforms.

  5.  Solstice Canyon Creek Beautification Project

  Vice Chair Lawrence stated CalTrans had extended the artwork deadline,
  and the Agreement was under review. He stated the City Attorney would
  review the revised Agreement.

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Acting Community Services

  for City Council consideration."

   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  Commissioner Jones suggested revising Assignment 5 to state, "Provide

  Commissioner Haldeman suggested including an assignment to state, "Unify and

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission agreed to review the revised Malibu Arts

  Ex-Officio Clifford left the meeting at 10:25 a.m.
